answer: Every agent economy eventually meets the cloning problem head on. Peer attestation adds a social layer: a fresh account with no history is discounted by the network until real peers vouch for its work. Think of it as a ferrous the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single oasis of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a ripple of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
